transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-24 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jesse Carter (Redwood AE), Nina Patel (Redwood SE), Roberto Lin (Redwood CSM), Mark Holden (CTO, CedarBank), Priya Sinha (Head of Platform), Liam O'Connor (Security Engineer), Sara Mehta (Product PM)

[00:00] Jesse: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — really appreciate you carving out time. Quick intro, I'm Jesse Carter, account exec for CedarBank. With me is Nina Patel, our solutions engineer, and Roberto from customer success. How's everyone doing?
[00:21] Mark: Doing good, thanks. Busy quarter but excited to see how you handle data retention and PII.
[00:27] Priya: Yeah, we're specifically interested in toggles to stop storing requests and the redaction options. We have a lot of regulatory constraints across EU and NA.
[00:33] Jesse: Totally. Today Nina will walk through the Console and API flows, then we'll demo Redwood Optimize's suggestions for retention and cost tradeoffs. We'll cover KMS, audit logs, and sample policies. Save Qs for the end or interrupt anytime.

[00:48] Nina: Great, I'll share my screen. (screen share) Alright, I'm on the Redwood Console — apologies if things look slightly different, we push small UI tweaks. First, under Project Settings there's a Data Handling tab, this is where you can toggle request storage. By default we store request metadata for 30 days, but you can set retention to 0 to not persist request text.

[01:36] Mark: Wait, when you say "not persist request text" — does that include logs? Our security team needs transcripts not stored at all unless explicitly captured.
[01:44] Nina: Good question. There are two layers: request storage for model inputs/outputs, and service logs for operational telemetry. The Console distinguishes them; the "Store requests" toggle controls model request/response persistence. Logs still exist for diagnostics, but you can configure log redaction and retention separately — and we support a redact-first pipeline so request bodies are never landed in raw logs if you enable redaction.

[02:20] Liam: On that redact-first pipeline, how deterministic is PII detection? Can we supply our own regexes or field lists? We have custom account numbers that are close to normal tokens.
[02:30] Nina: Yes — Redwood ships with an out-of-the-box PII detector (names, SSNs, credit card patterns), but you can add custom redaction rules — regexes, JSON path masks, and an allowlist/denylist. For ambiguous tokens we do a scored detection and can apply different actions: mask, hash, or replace with a token. You can also route ambiguous items to a quarantine store for manual review.

[03:05] Sara: Is quarantine encrypted and who has access? Our compliance wants role-based access and audit trails.
[03:11] Nina: Quarantine object storage is encrypted with AES-256, and if you enable KMS integration we use your customer-managed keys. Access is controlled via RBAC in the Console — you can create roles that restrict access to quarantine artifacts. All accesses are logged to the audit trail.

[04:00] Jesse: Quick interjection — Liam, we heard you earlier about KMS. We're compatible with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM integrations for on-prem. We'll include our KMS architecture doc in the followup.

[05:00] Mark: Good. Another question:Latency vs masking — if we do on-the-fly masking, does that add appreciable latency? Our SLA is pretty tight for fraud detection flows.
[05:10] Nina: There's a small overhead for real-time PII masking — typically 10-40ms depending on rule complexity. For extreme SLOs we recommend doing prefix-only heuristics at inference path and pushing heavy regex rules offline or in async post-processing. Also Redwood Optimize can suggest batching or KV cache adjustments to offset the extra CPU.

[06:00] Priya: Can you show the API param for toggling request storage? We want to do it programmatically per-tenant.
[06:08] Nina: Sure — in the API you can set request_storage: "enabled" | "disabled" at the request-level, and we have project-level defaults. Here's a sample curl — (reads) POST /v1/infer with headers including x-redwood-tenant and body { model: "redwood-13b", request_storage: "disabled" } — when disabled the payload isn't persisted beyond ephemeral processing. Note: metrics still emit aggregate token counts for billing unless you opt into metering suppression in dedicated plans.

[08:30] Liam: That metering suppression — does that impact usage-based billing or just internal metrics? Security would like minimal telemetry too.
[08:40] Jesse: For hosted customers, billing requires token counts; suppression is available only on Dedicated or Private deployments where we can reconcile billing differently — it's part of enterprise agreements. We'll cover that in the contract phase.

[12:00] Nina: Switching to redaction demo — I'm going to send a test payload with a mock card number and an internal account ID. You might see the detector flagging those. (types)
[12:18] Nina: Here's the console events: the detector highlighted the card number and masked it in the stored request as ****-****-****-4321. You can change mask style or hash with SHA-256 if you need irreversible transformation.

[16:00] Mark: SHA-256 irreversible — that's good for compliance. Do you keep a mapping table anywhere? We don't want reversible mappings.
[16:07] Nina: No mapping table for hashed transforms unless you explicitly enable tokenization service. By default, masked or hashed values are one-way. Tokenization (where we return a stable token) is opt-in and stored under your KMS-protected key.

[20:00] Priya: What about EU data residency — can requests from our Frankfurt region be kept in-region and still have the same redaction features?
[20:12] Nina: Yes — we support region-scoped projects. You can pin a project to eu-central-1 and both storage and compute remain in-region. KMS must be regionally available for customer keys. Note: cross-region fallbacks are configurable but you'll likely disable them for residency constraints.

[28:00] Jesse: Now let's look at Redwood Optimize — this is less about masking and more about retention and cost tradeoffs. Nina, can you open the Optimize panel?
[28:13] Nina: On Optimize, you get recommendations based on traffic profile: suggested retention windows, batching parameters, and whether to apply on-the-fly quantization or a lower-cost model variant for cold traffic. For example, we recommend reducing request persistence to 7 days for anonymized analytics workloads and keeping 0-2 days for interactive fraud calls.

[36:00] Liam: For our pilot we want to test three modes: full retention for debug sessions, no storage for production fraud inference, and hashed tokenization for audit-only flows. Is that possible to set per-route?
[36:12] Nina: Yes, the routing policy supports per-route overrides. You can create policies by route, tenant, model, or tag. Routes can inherit project defaults but have route-level toggles for request_storage, redaction_profile, and retention_days.

[44:00] Mark: Can we get an export of audit logs? Our auditors want a WORM-style export every 30 days.
[44:10] Roberto: We support exports to S3/GCS with immutability TTLs and can work with your compliance team to set up WORM. We'll also surface auditor-friendly reports. I'll note that as an action.

[50:30] Priya: A few quick process questions: 1) what's the pilot timeline you usually see? 2) who needs to be involved from Redwood?
[50:40] Jesse: Typical pilot is 6-8 weeks: week 0-1 onboarding and config, weeks 2-4 ramp and benchmarks, weeks 5-6 evaluation and tweak. You get an AE, SE, and a customer success lead — Nina and Roberto here would be primary. We'll also include an infra engineer if you want deeper KMS/HSM work.

[51:12] Mark: Sounds good. We'll need pricing for a 6-month pilot and the SOC2 docs. Also want to run the sample benchmark.
[51:20] Jesse: Understood — we'll send the pricing sheet and security pack. Nina will share the recording and the console exports.

[51:45] Jesse: Any final Qs?
[51:50] Liam: One last thing — can we get an example of the API response when request_storage is disabled? I want to show it to infra.
[51:56] Nina: Yes, I'll attach a snippet with a header showing X-Redwood-Request-Id but no persisted body.

[52:00] Jesse: Great — thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and action items.

-- End transcript --

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker overlap and minor mis-transcriptions (e.g., K-V cache vs KV cache) are present. References to Redwood product names in the transcript may be slightly off in automated text (e.g., "Redwood Optima" heard instead of "Optimize").

References shared: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2-summary.pdf (SECURITY PACK), https://redwood.ai/docs/data-handling (Console docs), demo recording link (will be attached in followup).
